name: Ultherapy Prime

lead: Ultherapy Prime is a newer version of the Ultherapy skin-lifting device. It uses focused ultrasound, guided by live imaging, to heat tissue beneath the skin at chosen depths.
It is used in clinics for brow, neck, under-chin and decolletage lifting. Published data on the Prime model are so far early case series and a survey.

paras: Focused ultrasound creates tiny heat points in the deep dermis and fascia, which is reported to stimulate new collagen and elastin and a tightening effect.
A 2025 survey compared patient-reported pain, redness and swelling between Prime and the older system. Treatment is performed by clinicians; the MFU-V category is FDA-cleared for several body areas.

lead: Ultherapy Prime is an updated version of the Ultherapy system, a noninvasive aesthetic device that uses microfocused ultrasound with real-time visualization (MFU-V) to tighten and lift skin. It is described in the literature as a second-generation system with an advanced processor and improved imaging compared with the original Ultherapy device.[1][2]

Microfocused ultrasound delivers energy to tiny points at different depths of the skin, producing thermal coagulation that is said to trigger a wound-repair response and the formation of new collagen and elastin.[3][4] A 2026 review states that MFU-V is cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration for brow lifting, neck and submental tightening and wrinkles of the decolletage, with additional clearance in 2025 for the abdomen and arms.[4]

In looksmaxxing culture the procedure is grouped with non-surgical hardmaxxing options for jawline and neck definition. Published evidence on the Prime model specifically is limited to early case series, a patient survey and company-linked comparison data, as listed below.
infobox: Updated model of the Ultherapy system (sometimes called MFU-V 2.0)[2]
Brow, submental and neck, decolletage; abdomen and arms (2025)[4]

paras: Ultherapy Prime uses ultrasound imaging during treatment so the operator can see tissue layers before delivering energy. A preprint comparing the original system with Prime reported that the newer device has enhanced visualization and reduced visual noise.[2] A published pilot case series describes Prime as having an advanced processor and improved imaging.[1]
Treatment areas described in a survey of patients include the brow, the lax submental and neck areas, and lines on the decolletage.[3]

Ultrasound energy is focused on small points at differing depths, creating thermal coagulation zones that are reported to induce neocollagenesis and elastin regeneration, producing a tightening and pulling effect in the deep dermis and fascia.[3][4]

A 2025 survey study compared patient-reported pain, erythema and edema after facial lifting with Ultherapy Prime and the older Ultherapy Legacy system.[3] A 2026 review of MFU-V discusses safety and technical considerations of the modality as a whole.[4]

A 2025 survey study compared patient-reported pain, erythema and edema between Ultherapy Prime and the Legacy system.[3] An Asia Pacific pilot case series described early experience with Prime, noting that published data in Asian patients had been lacking.[1] A 2025 preprint compared ultrasound visualization between the two systems and reported survey and case results from an early-experience program.[2]

Two trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov were recruiting at the time of writing: one examining long-term efficacy and duration of MFU-V at multiple depths (20 participants) and one examining visualization-guided treatment of the SMAS layer for facial laxity (50 participants).[5][6]
